ja: 対立・疎遠になった人々を和解させる
人と仲直りする、関係を修復する
矛盾して見える考え・要求・事実などを両立させる
不本意な事実・状況を受け入れる
帳簿・記録・数値を照合して不一致を解消する
en: to restore friendly relations between people or groups in conflict
to become friendly again with someone after a disagreement
to make apparently conflicting ideas, demands, or facts compatible
to accept an unpleasant fact or situation
to compare accounts, records, or figures and resolve discrepancies

nuance.ja: reconcile の中心には、離れているもの・対立しているもの・一致しないものを再び整合する状態へ戻すという発想がある。人についてはreconcile two partiesで両者を和解させ、be reconciled with someoneで人と仲直りした状態を表す。考えや要求についてreconcile A with Bとすれば、どちらかを完全に捨てるのではなく、両者が共存できる説明・方法を見つけることを意味する。reconcile oneself to somethingは、望ましくないが変えられない現実に抵抗するのをやめ、受け入れるという表現。会計のreconcile accountsは、帳簿・銀行明細・取引記録を比較し、差額や誤りの原因を確認して一致させる専門的な用法である。
nuance.en: The central idea of reconcile is bringing separated, conflicting, or inconsistent things back into agreement. With people, reconcile two parties means restoring friendly relations between them, while be reconciled with someone describes the resulting relationship. To reconcile A with B is to find an explanation or arrangement that allows both apparently conflicting elements to coexist rather than simply rejecting one. Reconcile oneself to something means ceasing to resist and accepting an unpleasant reality that may not be changeable. In accounting, reconciling accounts means comparing ledgers, bank statements, or transaction records and identifying the causes of discrepancies so that the figures agree.

ja: reconcile：対立する人・考え・記録を再び一致・両立する状態へ導く。
resolve：問題・紛争・疑問に解決を与え、未処理の状態を終わらせる。
mediate：中立的な第三者として対立当事者間の交渉・合意を支援する。
harmonize：異なる要素を調和させ、全体として円滑に機能させる。
settle：紛争・請求・問題について合意や決定に達し、決着させる。
en: reconcile: to restore agreement or compatibility between conflicting people, ideas, or records.
resolve: to find a solution to a problem, dispute, or question and bring the unresolved state to an end.
mediate: to assist opposing parties as a neutral third party in reaching an agreement.
harmonize: to make different elements work together smoothly as a coherent whole.
settle: to reach an agreement or decision that brings a dispute, claim, or problem to a conclusion.

etymology.ja: ラテン語 reconciliare『再び結び付ける、友好関係を回復させる』に由来し、古フランス語 reconcilier を経て英語に入った。re-『再び』と conciliare『結び付ける、好意を得る』から成り、conciliareはconcilium『会議、集会』と関連する。分かれていた人々を再び集めるという構造が、現在の和解・整合の意味に残っている。
etymology.en: Reconcile comes through Old French reconcilier from Latin reconciliare, meaning to bring together again or restore friendly relations. It combines re-, meaning again, with conciliare, meaning to unite or win over, which is related to concilium, meaning a council or assembly. The idea of bringing separated parties together again remains central to its modern senses.

note.ja: 紛争・請求・意見の相違に合意や決着を与える。関係の修復までは必ずしも意味しない。
note.en: To bring a dispute, claim, or disagreement to an agreed conclusion, without necessarily restoring the relationship.

note.ja: 異なる考え・規則・要素などを互いに調和するよう整える。
note.en: To adjust differing ideas, rules, or elements so that they work together consistently.

note.ja: 異なる要求・意見を受け入れられるよう、方法や条件を調整する。
note.en: To adjust an arrangement or position so that differing needs or views can be accepted.

note.ja: 対立・けんかを終えて仲直りする、reconcileより日常的な表現。
note.en: An everyday expression for ending conflict and restoring friendly relations.

ja: 譲歩や友好的な態度によって人の怒り・反発を和らげる
敵対的な人物・集団の好意や協力を得ようとする
対立する当事者の間を取り持ち、合意を促す
労使紛争などについて第三者として非公式な解決を支援する
en: to reduce someone's anger or opposition through concessions or a friendly approach
to gain the goodwill or cooperation of a hostile person or group
to help opposing parties reduce conflict and move toward agreement
to assist in the informal resolution of a dispute, especially as a third party

nuance.ja: conciliate は、対立相手に友好的に接する、譲歩する、安心させるなどして、怒りや警戒心を弱め、交渉や協力を可能にすることを表す。結果として完全な和解が成立することまでは含まず、関係改善のための働きかけに焦点がある。この点で、関係や矛盾を再び一致する状態にするreconcileとは異なる。労働・商事紛争ではconciliationが、第三者が当事者間の意思疎通を助け、自主的な合意を促す比較的柔軟な手続を指す場合がある。日常会話では動詞conciliateより、形容詞conciliatoryを用いたa conciliatory gestureやa conciliatory toneの方がよく見られる。
nuance.en: Conciliate means reducing another person's hostility, anger, or suspicion through a friendly approach, reassurance, or concession so that negotiation or cooperation becomes possible. It focuses on the attempt to improve the atmosphere and does not necessarily imply that a complete reconciliation has been achieved. This distinguishes it from reconcile, which emphasizes restoring an actual relationship or bringing conflicting elements into agreement. In labor and commercial disputes, conciliation can refer to a flexible process in which a third party assists communication and encourages the parties to reach their own settlement. In ordinary modern usage, the adjective conciliatory, as in a conciliatory gesture or tone, is more common than the verb.

ja: conciliate：友好的態度・譲歩によって相手の反発を和らげ、好意や協力を得ようとする。
reconcile：対立する人・考え・記録を、実際に一致・両立する状態へ戻す。
appease：要求を受け入れるなどして、怒りや攻撃を一時的に鎮める。
placate：怒っている特定の相手をなだめ、落ち着かせる。
mediate：中立的な第三者として、対立当事者の交渉と合意形成を支援する。
en: conciliate: to reduce opposition through friendliness or concession and seek another party's goodwill or cooperation.
reconcile: to restore an actual relationship or bring conflicting people, ideas, or records into agreement.
appease: to calm anger or aggression, often by satisfying demands or making concessions.
placate: to calm a particular person who is angry or hostile.
mediate: to assist opposing parties as a neutral third party in negotiating an agreement.

etymology.ja: ラテン語 conciliare『結び付ける、好意を得る、和解させる』に由来する。これはconcilium『会議、集会』と関連し、人々を一つの場へ集めるという観念を持つ。reconcileも同じ語にre-『再び』を加えたreconciliareに由来するため、両語は語源的にも密接な関係にある。
etymology.en: Conciliate comes from Latin conciliare, meaning to unite, win over, or bring into agreement. It is related to concilium, meaning a council or assembly, and carries the underlying idea of bringing people together. Reconcile derives from the related Latin reconciliare, with re- meaning again, so the two English verbs are historically as well as semantically connected.

note.ja: 怒っている人を、譲歩・謝罪・贈り物などによってなだめる。
note.en: To calm an angry person, often through a concession, apology, or favorable action.

note.ja: 相手の要求を満たすことで怒り・敵意を鎮める。過度な譲歩という批判的な響きを持つことがある。
note.en: To calm hostility by satisfying demands, sometimes with a critical implication of excessive concession.

note.ja: 人の怒りや不安を言葉・対応によって和らげる硬い語。
note.en: A formal verb meaning to soften someone's anger or anxiety through words or accommodating action.

note.ja: 説得や友好的な働きかけによって、反対者を味方・支持者に変える口語的な表現。
note.en: An everyday expression for gaining the support of someone who was previously doubtful or opposed.

patterns: do little / nothing to mollify + person
grammar.usage_note: The correct spelling is mollify, not molify.

ja: 怒っている人をなだめ、気持ちを和らげる
人の不安・懸念・不満を軽減する
謝罪・説明・譲歩などによって反発を弱める
痛み・厳しさ・激しさなどを和らげる
en: to calm someone who is angry or upset
to reduce a person's anxiety, concern, or dissatisfaction
to weaken opposition through an apology, explanation, or concession
to soften or reduce pain, harshness, or intensity

nuance.ja: mollify は、怒り・不安・不満などで硬くなった人の態度を、謝罪・説明・譲歩・好意的な行動によって柔らかくすることを表す。問題そのものを完全に解決したり、相手を味方に変えたりすることまでは意味しない。The refund failed to mollify the customer. なら、返金しても顧客の怒りを十分に鎮められなかったという意味になる。placateと近いが、mollifyは『感情や態度を軟化させる』ことに重点があり、やや文章語的。人だけでなくmollify concerns、mollify criticismのように、不安や批判を弱める意味にも使われる。語末が-yなので、三人称単数・過去形ではmollifies、mollifiedとなるが、-ing形はmollifyingとなる。
nuance.en: Mollify means softening the attitude of someone whose anger, anxiety, or dissatisfaction has made them resistant or hostile. This is often attempted through an apology, explanation, concession, reassurance, or favorable action. The verb does not necessarily imply that the underlying problem has been solved or that the person has become supportive. The refund failed to mollify the customer means that it did not sufficiently calm the customer's anger. Mollify is close to placate but particularly emphasizes softening feelings or attitudes and sounds somewhat literary or formal. It can also take abstract objects, as in mollify concerns or mollify criticism.

ja: mollify：謝罪・説明・譲歩などによって、人の怒り・不安・反発を柔らげる。
placate：怒っている特定の人に何かを与える・約束するなどして、直接なだめる。
appease：要求を満たすことで怒り・敵意を鎮めるが、過度な譲歩という批判を含むことがある。
conciliate：友好的な態度や譲歩によって反対者の好意・協力を得ようとする。
soothe：優しい言葉・接触・処置などによって、感情・痛み・刺激を穏やかにする。
en: mollify: to soften someone's anger, anxiety, or opposition through explanation, apology, or concession.
placate: to directly calm an angry person, often by giving or promising something desired.
appease: to calm hostility by satisfying demands, sometimes implying excessive concession.
conciliate: to seek an opponent's goodwill or cooperation through friendliness or compromise.
soothe: to gently calm an emotion, pain, or irritation through comforting words, contact, or treatment.

etymology.ja: ラテン語 mollificare『柔らかくする』に由来する。これはmollis『柔らかい』とfacere『作る、～にする』から成る。文字どおりには『柔らかくする』ことであり、物理的な硬さを和らげる意味から、人の怒り・態度・感情を軟化させる比喩的意味が発達した。emollient『皮膚を柔らかくするもの、場を和らげるもの』もmollisと関連する。
etymology.en: Mollify comes from Latin mollificare, meaning to make soft. It combines mollis, meaning soft, with facere, meaning to make or do. Its literal sense of softening something physically developed into the figurative meaning of softening a person's anger, attitude, or feelings. Emollient is related to the same Latin root mollis.

note.ja: 怒っている人を、譲歩・謝罪・贈り物などによってなだめる。
note.en: To calm an angry person through a concession, apology, gift, or other favorable action.

note.ja: 優しい働きかけによって、人の感情や身体的な痛みを穏やかにする。
note.en: To gently calm a person's feelings or relieve physical pain or irritation.

note.ja: 興奮・動揺・怒りを静める最も一般的で中立的な語。
note.en: The general neutral verb for reducing excitement, agitation, fear, or anger.

note.ja: 怒り・騒乱・抵抗を鎮めて平静な状態にする。集団や地域にも使われる。
note.en: To bring an angry person, disturbed group, or resistant area into a calmer and more peaceful state.

en: to move at the same speed as a person, vehicle, or other moving object
to deal successfully with the pace or amount of work, study, or demand

to stay informed about news, research, or current developments

nuance.ja: keep up with は、進み続ける人・物・状況に対して、自分も遅れない状態を維持することを表す。物理的には歩行・走行速度、比喩的には仕事量、学習、需要、技術革新、ニュースなどに使われる。catch up withが、すでに生じた遅れを取り戻して相手と同じ位置に到達することに重点を置くのに対し、keep up withは現在同じ位置・水準にあり、それを維持することが中心となる。keep up with paymentsでは支払いを期限どおり続ける意味になる。句動詞全体は分離できず、代名詞もkeep up with themのようにwithの後ろに置く。keep someone upは『人を寝かせない』という別の表現なので、語順に注意が必要。
nuance.en: Keep up with means maintaining one's position relative to a person, object, or situation that continues to move or develop. It applies physically to walking or driving speed and figuratively to workload, study, demand, technological change, and current information. Whereas catch up with emphasizes recovering an existing gap and reaching the same position, keep up with emphasizes remaining at the same pace or level. With payments, it means continuing to pay the required amounts on time. The expression is inseparable, so even a pronoun follows with, as in keep up with them. Keep someone up has the unrelated meaning of preventing someone from sleeping.

catch up with: to recover an existing delay and reach the same position or level.

etymology.ja: keep『保つ』、up『上の位置・水準に』、with『～と共に』からなる句動詞。文字どおりには、進む相手と共に同じ位置・水準を保つことを表す。そこから、物理的な速度だけでなく、変化・情報・仕事量・支払いなどに遅れないという比喩的意味が発達した。keepは古英語cepan『保つ、注意する』に由来する。
etymology.en: The expression combines keep, meaning maintain, up, indicating a continuing level or position, and with, expressing accompaniment. Its literal image is maintaining one's position alongside something that is moving. This developed from physical pace into the broader senses of remaining current with change, information, workload, and payments. Keep derives from Old English cepan, meaning to hold, observe, or pay attention to.

note.ja: 同じ進歩・成長速度を維持する。keep up withより形式的で、組織や経済の変化にもよく使う。
note.en: To maintain the same rate of progress or growth, more formal and common with organizational or economic change.

to keep one's knowledge current as laws, technology, or research changes

nuance.ja: stay abreast of は、変化し続ける情報や専門分野を定期的に追い、知識が古くならないようにすることを表す。特に法律、規制、技術、研究、市場、業界動向など、職業上の継続的な情報収集に適している。単に一度ニュースを知るのではなく、今後も最新状態を維持するという継続性を含む。keep up withより硬く、専門職・ビジネス・学術的な文章で使われやすい。stay abreast of competitorsのような場合は、情報を知るだけでなく、競争相手と同程度の進歩・能力を維持する意味にもなる。keep abreast ofもほぼ同義で、stayは最新状態にとどまること、keepはその状態を積極的に維持することをわずかに強調する。
nuance.en: Stay abreast of means regularly following a changing field so that one's knowledge does not become outdated. It is particularly suitable for laws, regulations, technology, research, markets, and professional developments. The expression implies continuity: it is not merely learning one piece of news but remaining current over time. It is more formal than keep up with and is common in professional, business, and academic writing. With competitors, it can mean maintaining comparable progress or capability rather than merely knowing what they are doing. Keep abreast of is nearly synonymous; stay slightly emphasizes remaining in the current state, while keep may slightly emphasize the effort required to maintain it.

ja: stay abreast of：専門分野・規制・技術などの最新動向を継続的かつ十分に把握する。

etymology.ja: abreast は中英語の表現 on brest『胸を並べて』から発達し、a-『～の状態で』と breast『胸』からなる。もともとは複数の人・船などが胸や船首を横一列に並べて進む状態を表した。そこから、他者や進歩と同じ位置を保つという比喩が生まれ、さらに最新情報・動向に遅れずついていく意味へ広がった。
etymology.en: Abreast developed from the Middle English expression on brest, literally at or beside the breast. It consists historically of a-, indicating a state or position, and breast. It originally described people or vessels moving side by side in a line. This physical image developed into the figurative sense of remaining level with progress or competitors and then remaining fully informed about current developments.

note.ja: stay abreast ofとほぼ同義。最新情報を把握するための継続的な努力をやや強く感じさせる。
note.en: Nearly synonymous, with a slight additional emphasis on the continuing effort to remain informed.

nuance.ja: stay current with は、知識・技能・技術・業務方法などが古くならず、現在の基準や状況に対応している状態を維持することを表す。stay abreast ofが最新の動向を継続的に把握する『情報収集』に重点を置くのに対し、stay current withは得た情報を知識・技能・実務に反映し、現在も有効な状態を保つことに焦点を置きやすい。withの後ろにはtechnology、standards、changesなど、追随する対象を置く。特定の話題について情報を把握する場合はstay current on the latest researchのようにonもよく使われる。また、keep one's skills currentのようにcurrentを目的格補語として使うこともできる。
nuance.en: Stay current with means maintaining knowledge, skills, technology, or working practices in a state that remains up to date and applicable under present conditions. Stay abreast of tends to emphasize continuously following developments and obtaining information, while stay current with often emphasizes incorporating that information so one's knowledge or practices do not become outdated. With commonly introduces a changing system or field, such as technology, standards, or regulatory changes. On is also frequent when referring to information about a particular topic, as in stay current on the latest research. Current can also appear as an object complement, as in keep your skills current.

stay abreast of：専門分野・規制・技術などの最新動向を継続的かつ十分に把握する。
stay up to date with：最新情報や変更を把握する、より一般的で日常的な表現。
keep up with：人・仕事・変化・情報などと同じ速度・水準を保つ。
catch up on：未読情報・未処理の仕事など、すでに生じた遅れを取り戻す。

stay abreast of: to remain continuously and fully informed about the latest professional or technical developments.
stay up to date with: the more general everyday expression for remaining informed about current information or changes.
keep up with: to maintain the same speed or level as a person, workload, development, or flow of information.

etymology.ja: currentはラテン語currere『走る』の現在分詞currens『走っている、流れている』に由来し、古フランス語currentを経て英語に入った。当初は水・空気などの『流れ』を表し、そこから『現在進行している』『現在通用している』という意味が生まれた。stay currentは、時間の流れとともに進み、過去の状態に取り残されないという比喩的な構造を持つ。
etymology.en: Current derives through Old French from Latin currens, the present participle of currere, meaning to run. It first referred to something running or flowing, such as water or air, and later developed the senses of presently occurring and presently accepted or valid. Stay current therefore figuratively suggests moving with the flow of time rather than being left in an outdated state.

note.ja: 最新の情報・変更を把握している状態を保つ、最も直接的で一般的な言い換え。

to attempt to obtain or achieve a job, prize, or goal

to attack a person physically or verbally

nuance.ja: go forの各用法には、選択肢・目標・活動・相手などへ向かっていくという共通のイメージがある。選択ではI’ll go for the blue one.のように、opt forより口語的で即決的な響きがある。目標についてgo for the championshipとすれば、積極的に獲得を目指すことを表す。命令形Go for it!は、迷っている人に『やってみなよ』『思い切って挑戦しなよ』と勧める表現。go for someoneは文脈によって、物理的に襲いかかる、激しく非難する、またはその人に魅力を感じるという意味になり得る。商品についてgo for $100なら100ドルで売れる・取引されるという意味。句全体は分離せず、go for it、go for themのように目的語をforの後ろに置く。
nuance.en: The senses of go for share the image of directing oneself toward an option, objective, activity, or person. In choice contexts, I'll go for the blue one is more conversational and spontaneous than opt for. With a goal, go for the championship means actively attempting to win it. The imperative Go for it! encourages someone to stop hesitating and make the attempt. Go for someone can mean physically attack, criticize aggressively, or, depending on the context, find that type of person attractive. When an item goes for one hundred dollars, it sells or is offered at that price. The construction is inseparable, and its object follows for, as in go for it.

ja: go for：口語的に選択肢を選ぶ、または目標の獲得へ積極的に向かう。
opt for：複数の選択肢を検討したうえで一つを選ぶ、やや形式的な表現。
choose：人・物・行動などを選ぶ最も一般的で中立的な語。
aim for：目標として特定の結果・数値・水準を設定し、そこへ努力を向ける。
pursue：目標・利益・職業などを、ある程度の期間継続して追求する。
en: go for: to conversationally choose an option or actively attempt to obtain a goal.
opt for: to choose one alternative after consideration, in a somewhat more formal register.
choose: the general neutral verb for selecting a person, thing, or course of action.
aim for: to set a particular result, figure, or level as a target and direct effort toward it.
pursue: to continue seeking a goal, benefit, or career over a period of time.

etymology.ja: go『行く、進む』とfor『～を求めて、～に向かって』からなる表現。もともとの『ある物を得るためにそちらへ向かう』という空間的・目的的な意味から、『選ぶ』『獲得を目指す』『攻撃する』などへ広がった。価格の用法は、商品が特定の金額と引き換えに買い手のもとへ行くという取引の発想に基づく。
etymology.en: Go for combines go, meaning to move or proceed, with for, indicating a purpose, object, or direction. From the literal idea of moving toward something in order to obtain it, the expression developed the senses of choosing, attempting to achieve, and attacking. Its price sense reflects the idea of an item being exchanged or sold for a stated amount.

note.ja: 選ぶことを表す一般的な語。go forの口語的・積極的な響きは必須ではない。
note.en: The general verb for making a choice, without the conversational or energetic tone of go for.

note.ja: 選択肢を比較・検討して選ぶ。go forより形式的。
note.en: To select an alternative after consideration, sounding more formal than go for.

note.ja: 仕事・賞・地位などを得ようと試みる。結果が不確実であることを示す。
note.en: To attempt to obtain a job, prize, or position, emphasizing that success is uncertain.

note.ja: 目標・機会・方針などを積極的かつ継続的に追求する。
note.en: To actively and continuously seek a goal, opportunity, or course of action.

ja: go for the cheaper option — より安い選択肢を選ぶ
go for quality — 品質を優先して選ぶ

go for a drink — 飲みに行く

go for the title — 優勝・タイトル獲得を目指す
go for it — 思い切ってやる・挑戦する
go for someone — 人に襲いかかる・人を激しく責める
go for a high price — 高値で売れる
have a lot going for it — 多くの長所・有利な点がある
en: go for the cheaper option
go for quality
go for a walk
go for a drink
go for the job
go for the title
go for it
go for someone
go for a high price
have a lot going for it

ja: I think I'll go for the cheaper model. — より安いモデルにしようと思う。
She has decided to go for the senior position. — 彼女は上級職の獲得に挑戦することを決めた。
If you believe the idea will work, go for it. — その案がうまくいくと思うなら、思い切ってやってみなさい。
A similar painting recently went for more than a million dollars at auction. — 類似の絵画が最近、競売で100万ドルを超える価格で落札された。
The location is inconvenient, but the apartment has a lot going for it. — 立地は不便だが、そのアパートには多くの長所がある。
en: I think I'll go for the cheaper model.
She has decided to go for the senior position.
If you believe the idea will work, go for it.
A similar painting recently went for more than a million dollars at auction.
The location is inconvenient, but the apartment has a lot going for it.

patterns: fall behind in + work / studies / field

ja: 移動中にほかの人・集団より遅れる
仕事・学習・計画などの進捗が予定より遅れる
競争相手・業界標準・技術進歩などについていけなくなる
支払い・返済・提出などを期限どおり処理できなくなる
成績・順位・生産量などでほかより低い位置に下がる
en: to move more slowly and become separated from another person or group
to make less progress than expected in work, study, or a plan
to fail to keep pace with competitors, standards, or technological development
to fail to make payments, repayments, or submissions when they are due
to move into a lower position in performance, ranking, or output

nuance.ja: fall behind は、当初は同じ位置・予定どおりの状態にいたものが、速度・作業量・能力などを維持できず、相対的または予定上の遅れを生じさせることを表す。物理的な移動、勉強・仕事、納期、競争、支払いなどに広く使える。fall behind on paymentsは支払期限を守れず滞納が生じること、fall behind scheduleは計画が予定より遅れることを意味する。lag behindも近いが、lagは他者や基準と比較して継続的に遅れている状態を客観的に述べやすく、fall behindは遅れが発生する変化に焦点を置く。反対方向の表現はkeep up with、発生した遅れを取り戻すことはcatch upで表す。
nuance.en: Fall behind describes a change from being level, current, or on schedule to being at a disadvantage because one cannot maintain the required speed, workload, or standard. It applies broadly to physical movement, study, work, deadlines, competition, and payments. To fall behind on payments is to miss due payments and begin accumulating arrears, while to fall behind schedule is to progress more slowly than planned. Lag behind is similar but often describes an existing and continuing comparative gap more objectively; fall behind emphasizes the development of that gap. Keep up with expresses maintaining pace, and catch up expresses recovering after a delay has arisen.

ja: fall behind：同じ位置・予定どおりの状態から、速度や進捗を維持できず遅れが生じる。
lag behind：人・基準・他国などより低い水準で遅れた状態が続く。
get behind：仕事・支払いなどがたまり、処理の遅れた状態になる口語的な表現。
trail：競争・選挙・試合・統計などで、相手より後ろの順位・数値にいる。
be overdue：支払い・提出・返却などが所定の期限を過ぎている。
en: fall behind: to develop a delay or disadvantage after failing to maintain the required pace or progress.
lag behind: to remain at a lower or slower level than another person, standard, or country.
get behind: an informal expression for allowing work, payments, or obligations to accumulate unfinished.
trail: to be behind an opponent in a race, election, game, ranking, or numerical comparison.
be overdue: for a payment, submission, or return to have passed its required deadline.

etymology.ja: fall『落ちる、下がる』とbehind『後ろに』からなる句動詞。もともとは集団と一緒に進んでいた人が速度を保てず、物理的に後方へ下がることを表した。そこから、仕事・予定・支払い・競争などにおいて、必要な位置や水準より後ろになるという比喩的意味へ広がった。
etymology.en: Fall behind combines fall, meaning to move downward or lose position, with behind, meaning at the rear. It originally described a person who could not maintain the group's speed and moved physically toward the back. This developed into the figurative senses of losing one's required position in work, schedules, payments, competition, or progress.

note.ja: 進歩・成績・能力などが比較対象より遅れた状態にあることを表す。
note.en: To remain slower or less advanced than a comparison group in progress, performance, or capability.

note.ja: 仕事や支払いを予定どおり処理できず、未処理分をためる日常的な表現。
note.en: An everyday expression for accumulating unfinished work or unpaid obligations.

note.ja: 競争相手に対して、それまでの地位・優位性・進展を失う。
note.en: To lose a previous position, advantage, or progress relative to a competitor.

note.ja: 集団・順位の中で後方へ下がる。物理的な移動や競技で特によく使う。
note.en: To move into a position farther back in a group or ranking, especially in movement or sport.

ja: fall behind schedule — 予定より遅れる
fall behind in one's work — 仕事が遅れる
fall behind in one's studies — 勉強が遅れる
fall behind on payments — 支払いを滞納する
fall behind with assignments — 課題の提出が遅れる
fall behind competitors — 競争相手に後れを取る
fall behind technologically — 技術面で後れを取る
fall further behind — さらに遅れる
fall badly behind — 大幅に遅れる
begin to fall behind — 遅れ始める
en: fall behind schedule
fall behind in one's work
fall behind in one's studies
fall behind on payments
fall behind with assignments
fall behind competitors
fall behind technologically
fall further behind
fall badly behind
begin to fall behind

ja: I slowed down and soon fell behind the rest of the group. — 私は速度を落とし、間もなく集団のほかの人たちから遅れた。
The project has fallen three weeks behind schedule. — その事業は予定より3週間遅れている。
She missed several classes and began to fall behind in her studies. — 彼女は何度か授業を欠席し、勉強が遅れ始めた。
The company risks falling behind its international competitors. — その会社は海外の競争相手に後れを取る危険がある。
He fell behind on his mortgage payments after losing his job. — 彼は失職後、住宅ローンの支払いを滞納した。
en: I slowed down and soon fell behind the rest of the group.
The project has fallen three weeks behind schedule.
She missed several classes and began to fall behind in her studies.
The company risks falling behind its international competitors.
He fell behind on his mortgage payments after losing his job.

patterns: fall in with the wrong crowd
fall in with someone's wishes / demands
be willing / reluctant to fall in with + noun
happen to fall in with + person

ja: 人・集団と偶然知り合い、行動を共にするようになる
人・集団と親しく付き合う、仲間に加わる
計画・提案・要求などを受け入れて従う
人の意向・希望に反対せず合わせる
en: to meet someone or a group by chance and begin accompanying them
to become friendly or associate with a person or group
to accept and follow a plan, suggestion, or demand
to accommodate oneself to another person's wishes or intentions

nuance.ja: fall in withには主に二つの用法がある。人を目的語にする場合は、偶然出会った人や集団と付き合い始め、その影響を受けるようになることを表す。特にfall in with the wrong crowdは、好ましくない仲間と付き合い始める定型表現である。計画・要求・意向を目的語にする場合は、それに同意して従うことを表すが、自分から熱心に支持するというより、相手に合わせて受け入れる響きがある。現代の日常会話では比較的まれで、人との関係ならstart hanging around with、提案への同意ならgo along withの方が一般的。fall in line withは別表現で、『規則・方針・基準に一致する、従う』という組織的な服従・整合を表す。
nuance.en: Fall in with has two principal uses. With a person or group as its object, it means meeting or beginning to associate with them, sometimes becoming subject to their influence. Fall in with the wrong crowd is a common fixed expression for beginning to associate with undesirable companions. With a plan, demand, or wish, it means accepting and complying with it, often suggesting accommodation rather than enthusiastic support. The expression is relatively uncommon in everyday modern English; start hanging around with is more usual for social association, and go along with for accepting a proposal. Fall in line with is a separate expression emphasizing conformity to a rule, policy, or standard.

ja: fall in with：人・集団と付き合い始める、または計画・意向を受け入れて合わせる。
go along with：提案・計画・決定に反対せず同意・協力する、より一般的な表現。
associate with：人・集団と継続的な関係や交流を持つ中立的な語。
comply with：法律・規則・要求などに従う、形式的で義務性の強い語。
fall in line with：方針・規則・基準などに従い、自分の行動や立場を一致させる。
en: fall in with: to begin associating with a person or group, or accommodate oneself to a plan or wish.
go along with: to agree or cooperate with a proposal, plan, or decision without opposing it, more commonly.
associate with: the neutral term for maintaining social or professional contact with a person or group.
comply with: to act according to a law, rule, or requirement, with a stronger formal sense of obligation.
fall in line with: to conform one's conduct or position to a policy, rule, or standard.

etymology.ja: fall『ある状態に入る』、in『中へ』、with『～と共に』からなる表現。ここでfallは物理的に落下する意味ではなく、fall asleepやfall into conversationと同様に、意図せず、または自然な成り行きである状態へ入ることを表す。人と同じ集団・隊列に入るというイメージから、仲間になる意味が生じ、さらに人の計画や意向と足並みをそろえる意味へ広がった。
etymology.en: The expression combines fall, in the sense of entering a state, with in and with. Fall does not indicate physical descent here; as in fall asleep or fall into conversation, it suggests entering a situation naturally or without deliberate planning. The image of joining the same company or formation as another person developed into the social sense and then into the sense of aligning oneself with another person's plan or wishes.

note.ja: 提案・決定などを受け入れて協力する。現代の日常英語ではfall in withより一般的。
note.en: To accept and cooperate with a proposal or decision, more common than fall in with in modern everyday English.

note.ja: 人・集団と交際・交流する。偶然仲間になるという含みはない。
note.en: To have social or professional contact with a person or group, without implying a chance encounter.

note.ja: 人・集団と合流し、一緒に活動する比較的口語的な表現。
note.en: A relatively informal expression meaning to join a person or group and act together.

note.ja: 不満や反対があっても、決定・状況を消極的に受け入れる硬い表現。
note.en: A formal expression for passively accepting a decision or situation despite reservations.

equivalents.fr: se joindre à / se conformer à

ja: fall in with a group — ある集団の仲間になる
fall in with new friends — 新しい友人たちと付き合い始める
fall in with the wrong crowd — 好ましくない仲間と付き合い始める
fall in with criminals — 犯罪者たちの仲間になる
fall in with someone's plan — 人の計画を受け入れる
fall in with a suggestion — 提案に同意して従う
fall in with someone's wishes — 人の希望に合わせる
fall in with someone's demands — 人の要求を受け入れる
be willing to fall in with — ～に合わせる意思がある
reluctantly fall in with — 不本意ながら～に従う
en: fall in with a group
fall in with new friends
fall in with the wrong crowd
fall in with criminals
fall in with someone's plan
fall in with a suggestion
fall in with someone's wishes
fall in with someone's demands
be willing to fall in with
reluctantly fall in with

ja: During his travels, he fell in with a group of artists. — 旅行中、彼はある芸術家の集団と知り合い、行動を共にするようになった。
His parents worried that he had fallen in with the wrong crowd. — 両親は彼が好ましくない仲間と付き合い始めたのではないかと心配した。
The committee eventually fell in with the chairperson's proposal. — 委員会は最終的に議長の提案を受け入れた。
She was unwilling to fall in with their demands. — 彼女は彼らの要求に従うつもりはなかった。
We fell in with two other travelers and continued the journey together. — 私たちは別の旅行者二人と知り合い、その後一緒に旅を続けた。
en: During his travels, he fell in with a group of artists.
His parents worried that he had fallen in with the wrong crowd.
The committee eventually fell in with the chairperson's proposal.
She was unwilling to fall in with their demands.
We fell in with two other travelers and continued the journey together.

related.responsibility_construction: it falls to someone to do something
related.beginning_construction: fall to work / fall to doing something

patterns: it falls to + person + to do
the responsibility / task falls to + person
a number / rate falls to + level
a city / organization falls to + enemy

ja: ある仕事・責任・決定を行う役目が人に回ってくる
数値・価格・割合などが特定の水準まで下がる
仕事・食事・議論などに勢いよく取りかかる
都市・組織・人物などが敵に敗北・占領される
財産・地位・権利などが特定の人の所有・担当になる
en: for a duty, responsibility, or decision to become a particular person's task
for a number, price, or rate to decrease to a particular level
to begin working, eating, or doing another activity energetically
for a city, organization, or person to be defeated or captured by an enemy
for property, a title, or a right to pass to a particular person

nuance.ja: It falls to someone to do somethingは、状況・制度・役割分担などの結果として、その人が仕事や責任を引き受ける立場になることを表す。本人が自由に選んだというより、『結局その役目がその人に回ってきた』という響きがある。数値を伴うfall to 20 percentは『20パーセントまで下がる』であり、fall by 20 percent『20パーセント下がる』とは区別が必要。fall to workやfall to discussing the problemは、少し古風・文学的に、活動へすぐ勢いよく取りかかることを表す。The city fell to the enemyでは敵に占領されること、The estate fell to his daughterでは財産が娘の所有となることを意味する。どの意味かはtoの後ろの語によって判断する。
nuance.en: It falls to someone to do something means that circumstances, rules, or the division of roles make that person responsible for the task. It often suggests that the duty has ultimately come to that person rather than being freely chosen. With figures, fall to 20 percent means reach the lower level of 20 percent and must be distinguished from fall by 20 percent, which describes the amount of decrease. Fall to work or fall to discussing the problem is somewhat literary or old-fashioned and means beginning energetically or immediately. A city that falls to the enemy is captured, while an estate that falls to a daughter passes into her possession. The object following to normally determines the intended sense.

ja: it falls to someone to do：状況や役割分担の結果、ある仕事を行う責任がその人に回ってくる。
it is up to someone to do：決定・行動をするかどうかが、その人の判断や責任に委ねられている。
someone is assigned to do：権限を持つ者によって、特定の仕事を正式に割り当てられる。
fall to a level：数値が特定の低い水準に達する。fall byは下落幅を表す。
fall to doing：活動にすぐ取りかかる。fall into doingは意図せず習慣・状態に入り込む。
en: it falls to someone to do: circumstances or assigned roles cause a duty to become that person's responsibility.
it is up to someone to do: the decision or responsibility for acting is left to that person's judgment.
someone is assigned to do: a task is formally given to someone by a person or body with authority.
fall to a level: to reach a particular lower figure; fall by expresses the amount of decrease.
fall to doing: to begin an activity immediately; fall into doing suggests unintentionally entering a habit or pattern.

etymology.ja: fall『落ちる、ある状態になる』と前置詞to『～へ、～に』の組み合わせ。物が人のところへ落ちるというイメージから、責任・財産・役目がその人に帰属する意味が生じた。また、低い地点へ落ちる物理的な意味から数値の低下や敵の手に落ちる意味が発達した。活動へ身を投じるイメージから、fall to work『仕事に取りかかる』という用法も生まれた。
etymology.en: The expression combines fall, meaning to descend or enter a state, with to, indicating a destination or recipient. The image of something falling to a person developed into the senses of responsibility, property, or a role passing to that person. Physical descent produced the numerical sense and the idea of falling into an enemy's hands. The image of throwing oneself into an activity also produced fall to work.

note.ja: 仕事・判断の責任が人に帰属することを直接説明する表現。
note.en: A direct paraphrase for a task or decision becoming a particular person's responsibility.

note.ja: 責任・権限・義務が人に移ることを表す非常に硬い表現。
note.en: A highly formal expression meaning for responsibility, authority, or duty to pass to someone.

note.ja: 数値・水準が特定の低い値まで下がる、fall toよりやや日常的な表現。
note.en: A slightly more everyday expression for a figure or level decreasing to a particular value.

note.ja: 必要な仕事に本格的に取りかかる。fall to workより現代的で一般的。
note.en: To begin working seriously on a task, more current and common than fall to work.

ja: it falls to me to decide — 決定する役目が私に回ってくる
the responsibility falls to someone — 責任が人に帰属する
the task falls to the committee — その任務が委員会の担当になる
sales fall to a new low — 売上が新たな最低水準まで落ちる
the rate falls to five percent — 比率が5パーセントまで下がる
fall to work — 仕事に取りかかる
fall to discussing the issue — その問題の議論に取りかかる
fall to the enemy — 敵の手に落ちる
the title falls to someone — 地位・称号が人に引き継がれる
the estate falls to an heir — 財産が相続人のものになる
en: it falls to me to decide
the responsibility falls to someone
the task falls to the committee
sales fall to a new low
the rate falls to five percent
fall to work
fall to discussing the issue
fall to the enemy
the title falls to someone
the estate falls to an heir

ja: It falls to the chairperson to make the final decision. — 最終決定を下す役目は議長にある。
After the manager resigned, responsibility for the project fell to me. — 管理者の辞任後、その事業の責任は私に回ってきた。
The unemployment rate fell to 3.5 percent. — 失業率は3.5パーセントまで低下した。
After a short break, everyone fell to work. — 短い休憩の後、全員が勢いよく仕事に取りかかった。
The fortress eventually fell to the invading army. — その要塞は最終的に侵攻軍の手に落ちた。
en: It falls to the chairperson to make the final decision.
After the manager resigned, responsibility for the project fell to me.
The unemployment rate fell to 3.5 percent.
After a short break, everyone fell to work.
The fortress eventually fell to the invading army.

patterns: fall under the jurisdiction of + authority

ja: 特定の分類・項目・定義に該当する
法律・規則・条項などの適用範囲に入る
裁判所・行政機関などの管轄に属する
人・組織・国家などの支配・影響下に入る
疑い・監視・批判・攻撃などの対象となる
en: to belong to a particular category, heading, or definition
to be covered by a law, regulation, provision, or rule
to be within the jurisdiction of a court or authority
to come under the control or influence of a person, organization, or state
to become subject to suspicion, scrutiny, criticism, or attack

nuance.ja: fall under は、ある対象が上位の分類・規則・権限・影響力の『下に入る』ことを表す。法律文脈では、ある行為や商品が特定の条項・定義・例外に該当することを述べる際に使われる。The conduct falls under Article 5. なら、その行為に第5条が適用される、または第5条に分類されるという意味になる。fall under the jurisdiction of a courtは裁判所の管轄に属することを表す。支配や影響については、以前は独立していたものが新たにその影響下へ入ったという変化を感じさせることがある。fall under suspicionやfall under scrutinyでは、疑い・厳しい調査の対象となることを意味する。句全体は分離せず、fall it underとはしない。
nuance.en: Fall under places something beneath a broader category, rule, authority, or influence. In legal writing, it is used to state that conduct, goods, or circumstances are covered by a particular provision, definition, or exception. The conduct falls under Article 5 means that Article 5 applies to or classifies the conduct. Fall under the jurisdiction of a court indicates that the matter is within that court's authority. With control or influence, the expression may suggest a change from independence to subordination. Fall under suspicion or scrutiny means becoming the object of suspicion or close examination. The construction is inseparable.

ja: fall under：分類・法律・管轄・支配などの上位の範囲に該当し、その下に置かれる。
fall within：境界・定義・期間・裁量などの範囲内に含まれることに重点がある。
come under：適用・支配・批判などの対象になる。fall underより変化の急激さが弱く中立的。
be subject to：法律・条件・制限・リスクなどの適用や影響を受ける状態にある。
fall into：分類・状態・習慣などの中に入る。権限や上位規則の下に置かれる意味は弱い。
en: fall under: to be placed beneath and covered by a broader category, law, jurisdiction, or controlling influence.
fall within: to be located inside the boundaries of a definition, period, discretion, or other scope.
come under: to become subject to a rule, control, or criticism, often more neutrally than fall under.
be subject to: to be in a state where a law, condition, restriction, or risk applies.
fall into: to enter a category, condition, or habit, with less emphasis on superior authority or control.

etymology.ja: fall『落ちる、ある状態に入る』とunder『～の下に』からなる表現。物理的に上位の物の下へ落ちるという位置関係から、規則・分類・権限・支配などの抽象的な上位概念の下に置かれるという比喩的意味が発達した。ここでfallは必ずしも物理的な落下を意味せず、『ある範囲・状態に入る』ことを表す。
etymology.en: The expression combines fall, meaning to descend or enter a state, with under, meaning beneath. The physical relationship of moving below something developed into the figurative idea of being placed beneath a broader rule, category, authority, or controlling power. Fall here does not necessarily indicate literal downward movement but entry into a particular scope or condition.

note.ja: 規則・権限・批判・攻撃などの対象になる。fall underと非常に近く、より中立的に使える。
note.en: To become subject to a rule, authority, criticism, or attack; very close to fall under and often more neutral.

note.ja: 法律・保険・契約・規則などの適用対象に含まれることを直接表す。
note.en: To be included within the application of a law, insurance policy, contract, or rule.

note.ja: 特定の分類項目・見出しの下に正式に整理される。
note.en: To be formally placed beneath a particular category or heading.

note.ja: 特定の法律・原則・契約条件によって規律される。
note.en: To be regulated or controlled by a particular law, principle, or contractual term.

patterns: fall for the idea that + clause
be easily tempted to fall for + noun
grammar.usage_note: The object follows for: fall for him / fall for it, not fall him for.

ja: 人を好きになる、恋愛感情を抱く
人や物の魅力に強く引かれる
嘘・策略・冗談などを本当だと信じる
詐欺・宣伝・偽情報などにだまされる
誤った考え・説明を疑わず受け入れる
en: to begin to love someone romantically
to become strongly attracted to a person or thing
to believe a lie, trick, or joke
to be deceived by a scam, advertisement, or false information
to accept a mistaken idea or explanation without sufficient skepticism

nuance.ja: fall forの人を目的語とする用法は、相手の魅力に抵抗できず、自然に恋愛感情へ落ちていくイメージを持つ。fall in love withと近いが、fall forはより口語的で、恋に落ち始めることや相手に夢中になることを表しやすい。一方、lie、trick、scam、excuseなどを目的語にすると、見せかけを見抜けず信じてしまうという否定的な意味になる。Don't fall for it. は『それを信じるな・だまされるな』という定型表現。人を目的語にしても、信用できない相手の魅力にだまされるという二重の含みを持つ場合がある。句全体は分離できず、fall for her、fall for itの語順になる。
nuance.en: With a person as its object, fall for conveys being drawn by that person's appeal and naturally developing romantic feelings. It is close to fall in love with but is more conversational and often emphasizes the beginning of attraction or becoming captivated. With a lie, trick, scam, excuse, or false idea as its object, it means failing to recognize the deception and believing it. Don't fall for it is a standard warning meaning do not believe it or be deceived by it. Even with a person, the expression may sometimes carry a double implication of being misled by someone's charm. The construction is inseparable.

ja: fall for：人に恋愛的に引かれる、または嘘・策略を見抜けず信じてしまう。
fall in love with：人を深く愛する状態へ入ることを、より明確かつ中立的に表す。
be attracted to：外見・性格・考えなどに魅力を感じるが、恋愛感情や愛情とは限らない。
be taken in by：人の外見・説明・策略などに欺かれることに重点がある。
fall prey to：詐欺・犯罪・病気・悪影響などの被害者になる、より深刻で硬い表現。
en: fall for: to become romantically attracted to someone or fail to recognize and resist a deception.
fall in love with: to enter a state of deep romantic love, expressed more explicitly and neutrally.
be attracted to: to find someone's appearance, personality, or ideas appealing, without necessarily implying love.
be taken in by: to be deceived by a person's appearance, explanation, or scheme.
fall prey to: to become the victim of fraud, crime, disease, or another harmful influence, more seriously and formally.

etymology.ja: fall『落ちる、ある状態に入る』とfor『～を求めて、～に引かれて』からなる表現。恋愛の用法は、理性的な制御を失って恋という状態へ落ちる比喩に基づく。だまされる意味は、仕掛けられた誘惑・餌・策略に引き付けられ、罠へ落ちるというイメージから発達した。
etymology.en: The expression combines fall, meaning to descend or enter a state, with for, indicating attraction toward an object. Its romantic sense is based on the metaphor of losing rational control and falling into love. The deception sense developed from the image of being attracted by bait or an appearance and falling into a trap.

note.ja: 人を深く愛するようになることを直接表す。だまされる意味はない。
note.en: To begin to love someone deeply and romantically, without the deception sense of fall for.

note.ja: 人に強く夢中になるが、一時的・非現実的な熱中である可能性を示す。
note.en: To develop an intense attraction that may be temporary or based on an unrealistic view of the person.

note.ja: 人・説明・見せかけにだまされる。恋愛的な意味はない。
note.en: To be deceived by a person, explanation, or appearance, without a romantic meaning.

note.ja: 説明・言い訳などを信じるという口語表現。否定形のI don't buy itが特に一般的。
note.en: An informal verb meaning to believe an explanation or excuse, especially common in I don't buy it.

equivalents.fr: tomber amoureux de / se laisser prendre à

The email looks official, but don't fall for it. — そのメールは公式なものに見えるが、だまされてはいけない。
Thousands of consumers fell for the investment scam. — 何千人もの消費者がその投資詐欺に引っかかった。
I can't believe you fell for such an obvious excuse. — あれほど見え透いた言い訳を信じたなんて信じられない。

patterns: fall back on a backup plan
have something / someone to fall back on
be forced to fall back on + noun
grammar.usage_note: The object follows on: fall back on it / them, not fall it back on.

ja: 第一の方法が失敗したときに予備の方法を利用する
困ったときに蓄え・経験・技能などを頼りにする
ほかに選択肢がないときに人へ助けを求める
不本意ながら以前の方法・慣習・方針へ戻る
緊急時に備えた代替手段として利用する
en: to use a backup method when the preferred approach fails
to rely on savings, experience, or skills in a difficult situation
to seek help from someone when no better alternative is available
to return reluctantly to an earlier method, habit, or policy
to use something as a reserve option in an emergency

nuance.ja: fall back on は、最初から第一選択として使うのではなく、通常の方法や計画が利用できないときに、予備として残されていたものを頼ることを表す。fall back on one's savingsなら収入などが不足したため貯金を取り崩すこと、fall back on experienceなら明確な手順がない状況で過去の経験を頼りにすることを意味する。have someone to fall back onは、困ったときに頼れる人がいるという安心感を表す。一方、be forced to fall back on an outdated systemのように、不十分・好ましくない代替策しか使えないという否定的な響きを持つこともある。名詞・形容詞では一語のfallbackを用い、a fallback plan、as a fallbackとする。
nuance.en: Fall back on means relying on something kept in reserve when the normal, preferred, or original option is unavailable or unsuccessful. To fall back on one's savings is to use them because ordinary income is insufficient, while falling back on experience means relying on past knowledge when no clear procedure is available. Have someone to fall back on expresses the reassurance of having a dependable person in difficult circumstances. The expression may also sound negative when the available alternative is inadequate or undesirable, as in being forced to fall back on an outdated system. The related noun and adjective are normally written as one word: a fallback plan and as a fallback.

ja: fall back on：第一の手段が使えないとき、予備として残していた人・資源・方法を頼る。
rely on：通常から人・物・制度を信頼し、その機能や援助に依存する。
resort to：ほかの方法が失敗したため、好ましくないこともある最終手段を用いる。
turn to：助言・援助・解決を求めて、人・情報源・方法へ向かう。
default to：特に選択・設定を変更しない場合や判断できない場合に、標準の選択肢へ移る。
en: fall back on: to rely on a reserved person, resource, or method when the primary option is unavailable.
rely on: to normally trust or depend on a person, thing, or system for support or proper functioning.
resort to: to use a last method after alternatives fail, often one considered undesirable.
turn to: to seek help, advice, information, or a solution from a person or source.
default to: to move to a standard option when no active choice or workable decision is made.

etymology.ja: fall backは、軍隊が前方の位置を維持できず、後方の安全な位置まで退却することを表した。そこへon『～を頼りにして』が加わり、前方の計画が失敗したとき、後方に用意していた資源・人・方法へ退いて頼るという比喩的意味が生まれた。名詞fallbackも、この『後退して利用できる予備の位置』から、代替案・予備策を意味するようになった。
etymology.en: Fall back originally described troops retreating from a forward position to a safer position behind them. With on, meaning in reliance upon, it developed the figurative image of retreating to a resource, person, or method held in reserve when the forward plan fails. The noun fallback similarly developed from a reserve position into the modern meaning of a backup option.

note.ja: 人・制度・資源の援助や機能を信頼して依存する。緊急時や予備手段に限定されない。
note.en: To depend on a person, system, or resource and not limited to emergencies or backup arrangements.

note.ja: ほかの選択肢がなくなったため、最後の手段を使う。否定的な方法にもよく使われる。
note.en: To use a last remaining method because other options have failed, often with an undesirable method.

note.ja: 必要なときに援助・法的手段・資源を利用する非常に硬い表現。
note.en: A highly formal expression for using available assistance, legal remedies, or resources when necessary.

note.ja: 何かを予備の手段として利用することを直接表す一般的な言い換え。
note.en: A direct everyday paraphrase meaning to use something as a reserve option.

ja: If the negotiations fail, we can fall back on our original proposal. — 交渉が失敗した場合は、当初の提案を予備案として使える。
After losing his job, he had to fall back on his savings. — 失職後、彼は貯金を取り崩して生活しなければならなかった。
When the computer system failed, the staff fell back on paper records. — コンピューターシステムが故障したため、職員は紙の記録に切り替えた。
Experienced professionals have a body of practical knowledge to fall back on. — 経験豊富な専門家には、困ったときに頼れる実務知識の蓄積がある。
